chunks: From him, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from al-Qāsim ibn Burayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who rises at the end of the night while fearing that dawn may suddenly overtake him: should he begin with al-Witr, or should he perform the prayer in its proper order so that al-Witr is the last of it? He said: Rather, he should begin with al-Witr. And he said: I used to do that.

key_terms.آخِرَ اللَّيْلِ: the end portion of the night
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ عَلَى وَجْهِهَا: the prayer in its proper and normal order
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the Witr prayer, the concluding odd-numbered unit of the night prayer
key_terms.يَفْجَأَهُ الصُّبْحُ: dawn suddenly overtakes him before completion

ai.seo_question: If someone fears dawn is about to break, should he begin the night prayer with al-Witr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat al-layl at the end of the night. If a person fears that dawn may arrive before he completes the full prayer in order, he should begin with al-Witr first; the Imam عليه السلام also states that he himself used to act in this way.
